question.text: STT (Securities Transaction Tax) is applicable on:

answer.text: Exchange-traded currency derivatives transactions at prescribed rates
Exchange-traded equity and equity-derivative transactions only — no STT on currency derivatives

explanation.text: The Logic: STT is levied on exchange-traded equity shares (cash) and equity/equity-index derivatives. STT does NOT apply to currency derivatives, interest-rate derivatives or commodity derivatives. Currency derivatives have no STT charge — the policy choice is to keep cross-border hedging costs low. The Trap: A common error is to assume STT applies to all exchange-traded derivatives. It only applies to the equity bucket. OTC forex and NDS-OM (G-sec) trades are also outside STT. Cross-Exam Context: STT applicability is tested in Series I (currency), Series IV (IRD) and Series VIII (equity). Each series asks the question from its own product angle. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Currency-derivatives traders see brokerage, exchange charges, SEBI fee, GST and stamp duty — but no STT. That cost gap is one reason currency F&O attracts large-volume hedgers.
